key_insight: The paper makes stress-based unit-cell optimization practical for the AHBR range-separated hybrid vdW functional by porting it from Quantum Espresso to VASP, enabling more robust structure prediction for complex matter.
engineering_relevance: This improves high-accuracy DFT workflows for materials discovery by combining reliable geometry optimization with a functional that can capture both cohesion and noncovalent interactions.
method: Ported the AHBR exchange-correlation functional from QE to VASP.
Validated the implementation on molecular interactions and simple bulk structure/cohesion benchmarks.
Applied it to difficult structure-prediction cases in distorted-rocksalt metal monoxides and the C2N COF.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports cross-code comparisons between AHBR-QE and AHBR-VASP for noncovalent molecular interactions, bulk structure and cohesion, plus application to magnetic and layered soft-matter systems.
watch_item: The main concern is implementation-specific robustness: the original QE setup did not support stable stress-based optimization for RSHs, so portability and numerical consistency must be checked carefully.
paper_title: Stress-based structure optimization for a range-separated hybrid van der Waals density functional
